overview: Black answers 2.f4 with the counterblow 2...f5, so that after 3.exf5 White wins a pawn and Black must regain it with ...exf4 or ...Qh4+ at the cost of kingside safety. White can castle, bring the queen out with Qh5+ in some lines and use the open e-file and weakened black king. It is rarely seen above club level, and White keeps the extra pawn in several lines.

white_ideas.idea: Take on f5 and hold the extra pawn, then develop with Nf3 and d4
Use Qh5+ checks and the open e-file against the black king
Return the pawn only when it gives a clear lead in development

black_ideas.idea: Regain the f5 pawn with ...exf4 or ...Qh4+
Take the centre with ...d5 and ...Bd6 in the Symmetrical line
Use the exposed white king after Qh5+ and Kd1 pawn-sacrifice lines

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with pawns exchanged on e4/f4/f5
Black king stranded on e7 or in the centre after Qh5+

character.notes: Both sides have exposed kings, early queen checks and open lines; White can be given check ideas such as ...Qh4+ and Qh5+ with the king caught in the middle.

gambit.notes: After 2...f5 3.exf5 White is a pawn up; Black may regain it, but White can keep it with accurate play.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious for Black: 3.exf5 simply wins a pawn and Black has to prove compensation through exposed white king ideas that rarely materialise.

structure.notes: Pawns leave e4, f4 and f5 early, leaving open e and f files and diagonals.

approach.notes: A rare countergambit that strong players hardly choose; it scores through surprise.

level.notes: Not a good first repertoire pick (dubious); the tactics are concrete and best judged by understanding.

sublines_that_differ.name: Greco Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 f5 3. exf5 Qh4+
sublines_that_differ.how: Black checks at once and regains the pawn only at the cost of the queen being a target.

sublines_that_differ.name: Shirazi Line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 f5 3. exf5 exf4 4. Qh5+ Ke7
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gives up castling for a pawn-down attack on the open e-file.

character.reason: Early checks, open files and exposed kings on both sides.

gambit.reason: Black plays 2...f5 as a countergambit; White can keep a pawn after 3.exf5.

soundness.reason: Strong players view it as refuted or close to it.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off early and lines open for the pieces.

approach.reason: Seldom chosen by strong players; scores through surprise.

level.reason: Dubious, so never Beginner; the tactics are concrete.

plans.reason: Black plays for development and queen checks against the open white king.
